## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

```{r}
#| label: imports

library(ggplot2)
library(shiny)
``` 


```{r}
 radioButtons( 
    inputId = "distribution-type", 
    label = "Distribution Type", 
    choices = list( 
      "T" = 1, 
      "F" = 2, 
      "Chi-squared" = 3 
    ) 
  )
```

```{r}
plotOutput('plot')
```

```{r}
#| context: server
#| 
t_dist <- dt(-4:4, df=10)

x_min = -4
x_max = 4
df = 10
lower_critical_val <- qt(0.025, df=df)
upper_critical_val <- qt(0.975, df=df)
output$plot <- renderPlot(
ggplot() +
    xlim(-4, 4) +
    stat_function(fun=dt, args=list(df=df)) +
    labs(
        title = "t distribution"
    ) +
    stat_function(fun = dt, args = list(df = df), 
            xlim = c(upper_critical_val,x_max), geom = "area", fill = "red", alpha = 0.5) +
                stat_function(fun = dt, args = list(df = df), 
            xlim = c(x_min,lower_critical_val), geom = "area", fill = "red", alpha = 0.5)
)

```

```{r}
#| include: FALSE
#| context: server
# Create a base plot with the desired x-axis range
renderPlot(ggplot(data.frame(x = c(-4, 4)), aes(x = x)) +
  stat_function(fun = dt, args = list(df = 10), color = "blue", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = "t-Distribution (df = 10)", y = "Density")
)
```
